title: HTTP-only serving can still instruct browsers to upgrade resources to HTTPS
test: tests/serverIntegration.test.js · CSP asks browsers to upgrade requests to HTTPS only when the listener serves HTTPS and plaintext LAN relay is off
proof: On the unchanged code the test (it spawns the real server.js for each of four settings) failed on the first setting, LOCAL_HTTPS=false with ALLOW_INSECURE_TRUSTED_LAN_RELAY=false: 'upgrade-insecure-requests expected absent in: default-src 'self';base-uri 'self';font-src 'self';form-action 'self';frame-ancestors 'self';img-src 'self' data: blob:;object-src 'none';script-src 'self' 'nonce-...';script-src-attr 'none';style-src 'self';upgrade-insecure-requests;connect-src ...' (true !== false). Fixed in server.js: the directive is [] only when config.LOCAL_HTTPS && !config.ALLOW_INSECURE_TRUSTED_LAN_RELAY, otherwise null. The same test now passes for all four settings: absent for LOCAL_HTTPS=false (relay off or on), present for LOCAL_HTTPS=true with relay off, absent for LOCAL_HTTPS=true with relay on; HSTS follows LOCAL_HTTPS; the script nonce is present in script-src; and every other directive is identical across the four settings.
